spec.name: baseline_v1
spec.rationale: establish the incumbent: all 23 features, 2s window, RF300

spec.name: drop_absolute_angle
spec.rationale: Absolute-angle features encode mounting/zeroing convention, not gait, so they should not transfer across device revisions (7: per-file calibration, never corpus-wide). Predicts rev14 up and steady_confusion down.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8758 vs champion 0.8730 (+0.0028); below the 0.005 promotion margin

spec.name: wider_window_4s
spec.rationale: The dominant error is steady_confusion (88.8% of error rows, whole-segment misclassification, not boundary lag), and the population's slow-cadence tail (down to 0.13 Hz per DOMAIN NOTES §9) means a 2s window often spans under one full stride, giving noisy amplitude/correlation estimates that RF misreads for an entire segment; a 4s window covers full gait cycles on slow walkers (plausibly rev14, the worst per-rev score at 0.61) at the cost of more abstention only at transitions, which are already a small minority of total error.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8150 vs champion 0.8730 (-0.0581); below the 0.005 promotion margin

reasons: Not a repeat: ledger only has baseline (2s, implicit) and drop_absolute_angle (also 2s); no prior window_s experiment exists.
Single-variable change: only window_s modified, drop_features and model_params empty — clean attribution.

Targets the dominant bucket: steady_confusion is 88.8% of error rows, and the mechanism (partial-stride 2s windows on slow-cadence gait producing noisy features that RF misreads for a whole segment) plausibly explains whole-segment misclassification, unlike transition-only fixes.

Consistent with DOMAIN NOTES §9, which explicitly flags window length as an open tradeoff and states 4s is needed for slow gait at the cost of more transition abstention — this is exactly what's proposed, not a contradiction of any established finding.

rev14 slow-cadence claim is appropriately hedged ('plausibly') rather than asserted as confirmed, avoiding overclaiming beyond what champion report shows (rev14 is worst-scoring rev, consistent but not proof of cadence cause).

spec.name: window_4s_stride_2s
spec.rationale: Clean re-test of the 4s window: hold stride at 2s so training-set size is comparable to the champion, isolating window length from sample count (the wider_window_4s run confounded the two, 5226 -> 2477 windows).

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8188 vs champion 0.8730 (-0.0542); below the 0.005 promotion margin

spec.name: drop_bad_band_frac
spec.rationale: band_frac is computed against a (0.5,3.0) Hz gait band that DOMAIN NOTES §9 says is wrong for this population (cadence down to 0.13 Hz), so for genuinely slow walkers it reads near-zero exactly like standing for the whole bout, feeding RF a persistent false-stand signal that matches the dominant steady_confusion bucket (whole-segment misclassification, not a boundary/lag issue) rather than a resolution problem the already-rejected wider-window changes targeted.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8711 vs champion 0.8730 (-0.0019); below the 0.005 promotion margin

reasons: Novel: no ledger entry touches band_frac/gait-band features (baseline, drop_absolute_angle, wider_window_4s, window_4s_stride_2s all target different fields)

Single conceptual change: drops one feature group (L/R angvel_band_frac pair), same precedent as drop_absolute_angle's multi-column single-concept drop; window_s and model_params left at champion defaults
Mechanism is grounded directly in DOMAIN NOTES §9 (0.5-3.0Hz band is wrong for a population with cadence down to 0.13Hz) rather than contradicting it

Correctly attributes to steady_confusion (88.8% of error rows, whole-segment misclassification) rather than repeating the already-rejected boundary/resolution fix (wider_window_4s, window_4s_stride_2s) that targeted the same rev14 slow-cadence symptom via a different, already-falsified mechanism

Weak spot, not disqualifying: neither band_frac feature appears in the champion's top-12 importance list, so the expected effect size on macro-F1 may be small — worth flagging in the run notes but not a reason to block

spec.name: regularize_min_samples_leaf10
spec.rationale: The dominant error bucket, steady_confusion (88.8% of error rows), is whole-segment misclassification under leave-one-rev-out CV, i.e. a generalization failure across subjects rather than a boundary/lag issue, and unconstrained trees (default min_samples_leaf=1) can carve leaves around training-rev-specific quirks (per-file offsets/calibration per DOMAIN NOTES SS7) that fail to transfer to a held-out rev like rev14 (0.61 F1, the worst); raising min_samples_leaf to 10 forces splits to rely on patterns shared across multiple subjects instead of memorizing single-rev idiosyncrasies.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8181 vs champion 0.8730 (-0.0549); below the 0.005 promotion margin

reasons: Novel: no ledger entry touches model_params/regularization; all prior tests changed features or window_s, not tree complexity.
Single change (min_samples_leaf 1->10), cleanly attributable.

Targets the dominant error bucket (steady_confusion, 88.8%) via a plausible mechanism: whole-segment misclassification concentrated on worst-generalizing rev14 (0.61) is consistent with unconstrained leaves memorizing per-rev idiosyncrasies rather than a boundary/lag artifact.
Does not contradict DOMAIN NOTES dead ends (signal-based sagittal detection, naive decimation) or any §7/§9 finding.

Caveat, not disqualifying: drop_absolute_angle already targeted the same 'per-file calibration leaks into training' theory directly and only gained +0.0028, so the calibration-overfit story has shown limited leverage before -- worth flagging in the report writeup, but min_samples_leaf regularizes overfitting generally (not just via those features), so it's a distinct enough mechanism to still be worth the run.

spec.name: drop_offset_only
spec.rationale: DOMAIN NOTES §10.1 directly measured ang_LR_offset's underlying descriptor (interleg_offset) at AUC 0.50 for walk/stand — it is posture-only noise for this task, not gait signal — yet RF's random per-split feature subsampling still occasionally builds leaves on it, encoding per-rev stance idiosyncrasies that don't transfer to a held-out rev and feeding steady_confusion (88.8% of error rows); this isolates that one zero-signal feature instead of the prior drop_absolute_angle test, which bundled it with genuinely gait-informative mean/absmean amplitude features and only netted +0.0028.

reasons: Not a repeat: drop_absolute_angle (ledger) bundled ang_LR_offset with 4 other mean/absmean features and only netted +0.0028 below margin — this isolates the single feature, which is the correct follow-up to attribute that result rather than a duplicate of it
Single-feature change satisfies attribution (contrast with the confounded wider_window_4s case the ledger already learned from)

Targets the dominant error bucket (steady_confusion, 88.8% of error rows) via a stated, plausible mechanism: RF's per-split feature subsampling can build leaves on a zero-signal feature, encoding per-rev stance idiosyncrasies that don't generalize under leave-one-rev-out CV
Consistent with DOMAIN NOTES §10.1, which directly measured interleg_offset at AUC 0.50 for walk/stand (posture-only) — no contradiction

Caveat lowering expected payoff, not grounds for rejection: ang_LR_offset does not appear in the top-12 importance list, so its marginal contribution is likely small; expect an effect size near or below the drop_bad_band_frac result (-0.0019), not a guaranteed win — still worth the cheap, clean test to settle attribution

spec.name: drop_angvel_dom_hz
spec.rationale: features.py's own comment says at a 2 s window the FFT bin width (1/window_s = 0.5 Hz) leaves the gait band's 0.13 Hz low edge unresolvable, so L/R_angvel_dom_hz quantizes any slow-cadence walker onto one of a few coarse frequency bins that a given subject occupies consistently, letting RF split on bin membership as a rev-identifying artifact rather than true gait content and feed steady_confusion (82% of error rows) under leave-one-rev-out.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8886 ties champion 0.8862 (+0.0024), but steady_confusion falls 0.884 -> 0.818 (0.066 >= 0.02); at equal accuracy, prefer the model that fails passively

reasons: Premise verified against stages/s2_ml/features.py: DEFAULT_WINDOW_S=2.0, GAIT_BAND_HZ=(0.13,3.0), and the code comment at line 58 literally states resolution 1/window_s leaves the low edge unresolvable at 2s — the rationale's code claim checks out, and correctly uses 0.13 Hz (not the debunked 0.5-3.0 Hz band).

Not a repeat: drop_bad_band_frac (rejected, -0.0019) dropped the sibling _spectral() output (band_frac) on a 'reads near-zero for slow walkers' argument; this targets dom_hz specifically on a distinct mechanism (coarse-bin quantization causing rev-identifying leakage under LORO), not the same claim restated.
Single conceptual change (drop one descriptor, both sides), consistent with the L/R-pair granularity already accepted in drop_offset_only and drop_bad_band_frac.
Targets steady_confusion, the dominant bucket (82% of error rows), satisfying the leverage check on bucket size.

Caveat, not disqualifying: L/R_angvel_dom_hz don't appear in the champion report's top-12 feature importances (cumulative ~0.856), suggesting modest average split usage — weakens confidence the mechanism is a major driver, but low aggregate importance doesn't rule out rev-specific overfitting on a handful of splits, so this is worth letting the gate settle rather than pre-judging.

No contradiction with DOMAIN NOTES; per §11.4, remember the gate will only confirm the metric, not this leakage story — don't promote the rationale into DOMAIN_NOTES on the strength of a macro-F1 move alone.

spec.name: drop_ang_mean_only
spec.rationale: L_ang_LPF_mean and R_ang_LPF_mean are dominated by each window's static angle bias, which §4.6 identifies as a firmware/mounting zeroing convention baked into the on-sensor Deg fusion rather than gait content, and §10.1 already showed the analogous relative-bias feature (ang_LR_offset, AUC 0.50) was pure per-rev posture noise whose removal cut steady_confusion and promoted the champion; the absolute per-side mean is the same kind of static-offset signal one level down, so isolating it (unlike drop_absolute_angle, which diluted the effect by bundling mean with absmean and offset together for only +0.0028) should further reduce the still-dominant steady_confusion bucket (0.820 share) without touching the amplitude/correlation features that actually carry gait information.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8926 vs champion 0.8886 (+0.0040); below the 0.005 promotion margin

reasons: Premise verified in stages/s2_ml/features.py:86: `{name}_mean` is the per-window arithmetic mean of L_ang_LPF/R_ang_LPF, i.e. the window's absolute sagittal-angle level — consistent with the rationale's claim that it reflects per-file/per-rev zeroing rather than gait dynamics (amplitude/shape features like _std/_ptp/_ang_LR_corr are untouched).

§4.6 supports the generalization: Deg is on-sensor fusion whose 'fusion parameters are a device property' that can differ by revision even with matching column names — legitimately extends the zeroing-convention argument from Hip_Deg to L/R_ang_LPF_mean.

Not a repeat: drop_absolute_angle (rejected, +0.0028) bundled this with absmean and ang_LR_offset and was explicitly diagnosed as diluted; this isolates the untested remainder (mean-only) exactly the way drop_offset_only isolated ang_LR_offset from the same bundle and got promoted — same de-confounding logic, different feature subset, run against the current champion (post offset-drop, post dom_hz-drop), so it's not stale.
Single conceptual change (L/R pair of one feature type dropped together), consistent with precedent (drop_angvel_dom_hz also dropped an L/R pair as one change).
Targets the dominant error bucket (steady_confusion, 0.820 share) per rule 3.

Caveat for the log, not a blocker: L_ang_LPF_mean/R_ang_LPF_mean don't appear in the top-12 importance list for the current champion, so raw RF importance is low; per §11.4 the mechanism (steady_confusion reduction) must actually be checked against the taxonomy output regardless of whether macro-F1 moves, not assumed from the rationale.

spec.name: drop_ang_absmean_only
spec.rationale: features.py computes _absmean as mean(|v|) over the RAW (non-demeaned) window values, so for the angle channels it is dominated by each window's static mounting/zeroing offset (§4.6: Deg is on-sensor fusion output carrying a firmware/mounting convention, not gait content) rather than oscillation, exactly like L/R_ang_LPF_mean (isolating that alone already got +0.0040, just under margin) -- but ptp already supplies a clean, bias-free amplitude feature (top-5 importance) so absmean's marginal information over ptp is mostly that same non-transferring offset term; the earlier drop_absolute_angle test bundled mean+absmean+offset together and only netted +0.0028, diluting rather than isolating the effect, so this untangles absmean on its own and predicts a further cut to the still-dominant steady_confusion bucket.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8912 vs champion 0.8886 (+0.0026); below the 0.005 promotion margin

reasons: Premise verified: features.py:89 computes absmean as np.abs(v).mean() over the raw (non-demeaned) window array, confirming it inherits the static offset the way the rationale claims.

Not a repeat: absmean has never been isolated alone in the ledger — drop_absolute_angle bundled mean+absmean+offset (+0.0028), drop_offset_only isolated offset (promoted), drop_ang_mean_only isolated mean (+0.0040, rejected). This is the one untangled leg of that original 3-way bundle.

Single conceptual change: drops one feature type (absmean) on both sides, consistent with how prior approved single-feature ablations (drop_offset_only, drop_ang_mean_only, drop_angvel_dom_hz) were scoped.
Leverage plausible: targets the still-dominant steady_confusion bucket (0.820 share) via the same offset-contamination mechanism that worked for drop_offset_only and partially for drop_ang_mean_only.

Evidence consistent with report: L/R_ang_LPF_ptp are verified top-5 importance (ranks 4-5) and bias-free by construction (range is offset-invariant), while L_ang_LPF_absmean doesn't even crack the top-12 and R_ang_LPF_absmean is marginal (0.0251, rank 11), supporting the 'mostly redundant with ptp/mean' claim.

Caveat, not disqualifying: absmean correlates with the already-tested mean (both offset-driven), and mean-alone underperformed (+0.0040, below margin) — plausible this nets a similarly modest, sub-margin gain, but that's a reason to expect a smaller effect, not a reason it's untestable or contradicts DOMAIN NOTES.

spec.name: drop_static_offset_family
spec.rationale: combined drop of the static-offset angle family (ang_LR_offset + L/R ang_LPF mean + L/R ang_LPF absmean); §4.6 per-subject zeroing bias, not gait. each helped alone but under margin -- test if gains stack. human-directed multi-feature test, bypasses the one-change critic rule.

spec.name: drop_offset_family_and_domhz
spec.rationale: stack the two promoted ideas: static-offset angle family (current champion drop_static_offset_family) + angvel_dom_hz (prior champion). never combined before. human-directed multi-feature test, bypasses the one-change critic rule.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8946 vs champion 0.8977 (-0.0031); below the 0.005 promotion margin

spec.name: max_features_full_split
spec.rationale: Default RandomForest max_features='sqrt' considers only ~4 of the champion's 18 surviving features at every split, a heuristic sized for hundreds-of-features problems; with just 18 features (after the promoted static-offset-family drop) that starves root-level splits of the dominant discriminators (ang_LR_corr, L/R_ang_LPF_std/ptp, all top-5 importance) some fraction of the time, so different bootstrap trees anchor their early structure on whichever weaker feature got sampled instead of the strongest one, plausibly producing the whole-segment, non-reversing steady_confusion errors (82% of error rows) rather than boundary noise; setting max_features=None lets every split see the full feature set, and this direction is consistent with min_samples_leaf=10 (more regularization) having already cost -0.0549 on this same dominant bucket, i.e. this pipeline currently favors less-constrained trees, not more.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8764 vs champion 0.8977 (-0.0212); below the 0.005 promotion margin

reasons: Premise verified: FEATURES has 4 channels x 4 stats (16) + ang_LR_corr + angvel_LR_corr + ang_LR_offset (3) + 2x(dom_hz, band_frac) (4) = 23 baseline features (matches baseline_v1); drop_static_offset_family removes exactly the 5 features this spec also lists, leaving 18, matching the rationale's count.

sqrt(18)~4.24 confirmed via grep: BASE_MODEL_PARAMS in experiment.py does not set max_features, so RandomForestClassifier falls back to its library default 'sqrt' (requirements.txt pins scikit-learn>=1.4, whose classifier default is 'sqrt') -- the '~4 of 18 features per split' claim is accurate, not asserted from memory.

Single change relative to current champion: drop_features exactly reproduces drop_static_offset_family's already-promoted feature set (not a new drop), so the only actual delta is model_params.max_features=None. Clean attribution.
Not a repeat: no ledger entry touches max_features; regularize_min_samples_leaf10 tested a different knob (leaf regularization) and is only invoked directionally, not claimed identical.

Targets the dominant bucket (steady_confusion, 82.3% of error rows per the champion report) with a stated, falsifiable mechanism (split-level feature starvation on a small feature set), consistent with Section 11.4's ask that mechanisms be checkable against the taxonomy after the run.
No contradiction with DOMAIN NOTES: max_features is an explicitly whitelisted ALLOWED_MODEL_PARAMS key, and nothing in the notes touches RF split-candidate sizing.

spec.name: drop_angvel_mean_only
spec.rationale: features.py computes _mean as the raw signed mean over the window for every channel identically (line 86); for angvel_LPF this is not gait amplitude (std/ptp/absmean already capture oscillation magnitude and dominate importance) but the window's net signed angular velocity, which for genuine symmetric swing gait should average near zero over a full stride and is instead dominated by gyro zero-rate bias/drift, a per-device/per-session calibration artifact analogous to the static angle-offset family already shown non-transferring (drop_static_offset_family, champion) rather than gait content, so it plausibly lets RF split on rev-identifying bias rather than true motion and feeds steady_confusion (82% of error rows) under leave-one-rev-out.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8894 vs champion 0.8977 (-0.0083); below the 0.005 promotion margin

reasons: Premise verified: features.py line 86 computes `_mean` as the raw signed window mean identically for every channel, including angvel_LPF - confirmed by reading stages/s2_ml/features.py:81-100.

Not a repeat: no ledger entry drops angvel_LPF_mean. Prior 'static bias' tests (drop_ang_mean_only, drop_ang_absmean_only, drop_offset_only, drop_static_offset_family) all targeted the angle (ang_LPF) channel or ang_LR_offset, never angvel_LPF_mean.
Single conceptual change: drops one feature family (L/R angvel_LPF_mean together), matching how prior single-family tests (e.g. drop_ang_mean_only) were scoped and evaluated.

Mechanism is plausible and distinct from what's already measured: gyro zero-rate bias is a real, established IMU phenomenon, and the rationale correctly distinguishes it from the Deg-channel static-offset mechanism (analogous, not identical) rather than conflating them.

Leverage is consistent with precedent: drop_offset_only showed a near-zero-importance, non-transferring feature (interleg_offset AUC 0.50) can still hurt steady_confusion via occasional harmful RF splits even without appearing in top feature importances - angvel_LPF_mean is similarly absent from the top-12 importance list here, fitting the same profile.

No contradiction with DOMAIN NOTES: Section 4.1's 'angvel is reliable as d(angle)/dt' concerns derivative fidelity, not zero-mean-over-a-stride assumption; gyro bias is not the same claim as the retracted yaw-drift (Section 4.2, which is about Deg_Z integration drift, not raw sagittal gyro rate).

spec.name: class_weight_balanced_subsample
spec.rationale: BASE_MODEL_PARAMS already trains every experiment with class_weight='balanced' (weights computed once from each LORO fold's pooled y), so re-proposing 'balanced' would be a no-op; 'balanced_subsample' instead recomputes weights per tree from that tree's own bootstrap draw, which should help the minority stand class (16.9% of windows, weaker F1 0.83 vs walk's 0.96, and the source of most steady_confusion whole-segment errors) when a given tree's bootstrap happens to under-represent stand relative to the fold-wide ratio the fixed 'balanced' weight assumes.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8997 vs champion 0.8977 (+0.0020); below the 0.005 promotion margin

reasons: Premise verified: stages/s2_ml/experiment.py:36-37 confirms BASE_MODEL_PARAMS already sets class_weight='balanced', so the rationale's claim that re-proposing 'balanced' would be a no-op is correct, and 'balanced_subsample' is a genuinely different, whitelisted option (experiment.py:108 lists all three).

Stand-class numbers in the rationale match the champion report exactly (812/4812=16.9% support, F1 0.83 vs 0.9641 walk), so the gap it targets is real and non-trivial (16.9% of windows, not a marginal bucket).

Not a ledger repeat: no prior entry touches class_weight; drop_features list matches the current champion's already-adopted drop_static_offset_family set, so relative to the champion baseline this is a single isolated change (class_weight only), consistent with the precedent set by max_features_full_split.
Does not contradict any DOMAIN NOTES finding (Section 9's ALLOWED_MODEL_PARAMS explicitly sanctions class_weight tuning; no established finding says balanced_subsample is a dead end).

spec.name: cap_max_depth_8
spec.rationale: steady_confusion (82% of error rows) is a whole-segment leave-one-rev-out generalization failure, and with unconstrained max_depth (the only unexplored structural-regularization axis; min_samples_leaf=10 and max_features=None each already hurt by tuning the wrong knobs) trees can grow deep enough to carve leaves on rev-specific feature-value conjunctions rather than stopping at the shared top-level splits the importance ranking already identifies (ang_LR_corr, L/R_ang_LPF_std/ptp), so bounding depth should force every tree to rely on those broadly-shared splits and cut whole-segment misclassification on held-out subjects.

decision_reason: macro-F1 0.8938 vs champion 0.8977 (-0.0038); below the 0.005 promotion margin

reasons: Premise verified: stages/s2_ml/experiment.py:36-37 BASE_MODEL_PARAMS has no max_depth key, so sklearn defaults to unbounded (None) - the 'unconstrained max_depth' claim holds.
Novel axis: no ledger entry has ever set model_params.max_depth; it is distinct from the two tried knobs (min_samples_leaf10, max_features=None), so not a cosmetic repeat of either.
Clean attribution: drop_features exactly matches the current champion's (drop_static_offset_family) with only model_params.max_depth=8 added - single-variable test against the live champion.
Leverage correct: targets steady_confusion, the dominant bucket (82% of error rows) per the champion report.
Feature-importance claim checks out: ang_LR_corr, L/R_ang_LPF_std/ptp are indeed the top-5 importances in the champion report.

Minor inaccuracy in rationale: max_depth is not 'the only unexplored structural-regularization axis' - ALLOWED_MODEL_PARAMS also lists min_samples_split and criterion as untried. Does not invalidate the mechanism but is an overclaim worth flagging.

Caution (not disqualifying): both prior hyperparameter-regularization attempts failed in opposite directions - min_samples_leaf=10 (more constrained, -0.0549) and max_features=None (less constrained, -0.0212) - so the pipeline's default RF complexity already looks near a local optimum. This tempers confidence the mechanism will pay off but is exactly what the metric gate, not the critic, should settle.
